frozen_evidence.q27_stop_reason: no Pareto improvement for 200 committed updates

matched_trace_findings.finding: All 300 Q2.7 proposals were accepted at full scale; 204 were projected, none backtracked, and the maximum removed fraction was 0.061954474913212966.
matched_trace_findings.implication: Hard guard rejection and gross projection removal are not sufficient explanations for failure.
matched_trace_findings.limit: A small removed norm can still remove a decisive direction, and accepted steps can remain badly conditioned.

matched_trace_findings.finding: Across the matched first 300 updates, Q2.7 mean gradient norm was 0.6491063152299998 versus 1.6458561620066656 for Q2.6, and mean step displacement was 0.007109983232836668 versus 0.011707618236309995.
matched_trace_findings.implication: The isolated subspace received about 39.4% of Q2.6's mean gradient norm and about 60.7% of its mean step displacement.
matched_trace_findings.limit: Norms do not measure alignment with the quantity objective.

matched_trace_findings.finding: Over 300 matched updates, layer.5.w1 displacement summed to 1.4912508140992016 in Q2.7 versus 0.8409923800762605 in Q2.6; layer.5.w2 summed to 1.5230342705711895 versus 1.0579959197731201.
matched_trace_findings.implication: The top FFN moved about 77.3% and 44.0% more respectively in Q2.7, so 'the top FFN simply did not move enough' is contradicted by the trace.
matched_trace_findings.limit: Displacement is not causal attribution and does not reveal whether Q2.6 needed those groups.

matched_trace_findings.finding: Successful Q2.6 moved both FFN matrices in every transformer layer substantially during the first 300 updates; attention value/output groups also moved, while token embeddings carried the largest summed absolute replay drift and Fisher-weighted drift.
matched_trace_findings.implication: Useful capacity and preservation risk appear distributed, with embeddings a high-risk candidate and cross-layer FFN/attention changes plausible contributors.
matched_trace_findings.limit: Groupwise drift fields are local diagnostics. They cannot separate useful learning from correlated movement without an intervention.

matched_trace_findings.finding: Q2.6 first passed the quantity gate at update 200 with operation and exact-request rates of 0.954; Q2.7 had zero syntax, operation, and exact-request success at updates 100, 200, and 300.
matched_trace_findings.implication: A 100-update pilot is not adequate because even the successful control had not passed then; update 200 is the cheapest existing discriminating checkpoint.
matched_trace_findings.limit: This is one seed and does not establish variance.

hypotheses.family: complete top transformer block while freezing embeddings
hypotheses.causal_mechanism: The top block's attention, FFN, and normalization components jointly reroute representations into the required quantity protocol while lower blocks and embeddings preserve the inherited language basis.
hypotheses.expected_existing_trace_signature: Successful Q2.6 should show decisive movement or replay-gradient interaction concentrated in layer 5 attention and FFN groups; Q2.7 should show usable top-FFN signal that lacks only attention-mediated routing.
hypotheses.falsifier: At matched update 200, a preregistered top-block arm still has zero syntax/operation/exact-request success or does no better than the Q2.7 hard top-FFN control while consuming comparable replay budget.
risks: Still imposes a binary boundary unsupported by the literature.
May move language damage into top attention or normalization.
A one-seed success would not establish the boundary as minimal.

hypotheses.family: top attention plus top FFN with frozen lower blocks
hypotheses.causal_mechanism: Attention projections in the top layer provide the missing routing degrees of freedom while the top FFN supplies the transformation already attempted by Q2.7.
hypotheses.expected_existing_trace_signature: Q2.6 top-layer attention value/output groups should co-move with quantity progress and Q2.7 top-FFN movement should be large but behaviorally ineffective.
hypotheses.falsifier: A top-attention-plus-FFN arm fails to produce nonzero syntax and operation at update 200 despite gradients and accepted steps comparable to Q2.6.
risks: Attention-only expansion may still omit lower-layer coordination.
The exact boundary can be tuned post hoc unless fixed prospectively.
Replay preservation in Q2.7 may not survive the added routing freedom.

hypotheses.family: distributed graded plasticity across all layers
hypotheses.causal_mechanism: Every layer retains some update capacity, but a fixed training-only importance profile makes parameters with strong old-replay sensitivity increasingly sticky and parameters with strong quantity signal relative to replay risk more flexible.
hypotheses.expected_existing_trace_signature: Q2.6 success should coincide with distributed cross-layer movement, Q2.7 should preserve replay but underfit, and high replay-risk groups such as embeddings should be separable from high new-task-relevance groups.
hypotheses.falsifier: A profile fixed before training fails to improve the update-200 quantity vector over Q2.7, or achieves quantity progress only by exceeding the unchanged replay boundary or later frozen language gates.
risks: Replay-gradient importance may miss language behavior outside the replay set.
Noisy importance estimates can create false safe regions.
Scaling after adaptive optimization and projection can change constraint geometry.
Damage may migrate to low-importance groups rather than disappear.

hypotheses.family: distributed sparse plasticity selected from training-only signals
hypotheses.causal_mechanism: A prospectively frozen cross-layer mask concentrates updates on parameters with high quantity relevance and low old-replay risk while leaving the base forward computation intact.
hypotheses.expected_existing_trace_signature: Q2.6 group movement should be distributed rather than top-local, and a joint relevance/risk score should select parameters across multiple layers rather than a single FFN.
hypotheses.falsifier: The selected mask is unstable across training-only resamples, collapses into one layer, or fails to improve quantity at update 200 without breaching replay.
risks: Mask selection can overfit the acquisition sample.
A binary sparse mask recreates a hard cutoff at finer granularity.
Learning the mask jointly adds memory and another optimization target.

hypotheses.family: parameter-efficient residual adapters or low-rank updates
hypotheses.causal_mechanism: Distributed trainable residual paths learn the new routing faculty while immutable base weights retain the inherited model; active-model gates determine whether the new paths interfere at inference.
hypotheses.expected_existing_trace_signature: Q2.7 should underfit despite low replay change, indicating that preserving base weights is useful but local shared-weight capacity is insufficient.
hypotheses.falsifier: Active adapters/LoRA fail quantity at matched update 200 or pass quantity only by failing replay/language screens; inactive-base preservation does not count as success.
risks: Architecture, serialization, deployment, and parameter-count semantics change.
Task-specific paths may require a selector inconsistent with one-model operation.
LoRA can forget comparably to full fine-tuning in some language regimes.

hypotheses.family: selective embedding or output adaptation with replay regularization
hypotheses.causal_mechanism: Token representations or output logits may directly encode the missing syntax and exact serialization, so selective adaptation there could unlock behavior without broad hidden-state changes.
hypotheses.expected_existing_trace_signature: Q2.6 embeddings/output groups should align with gate transitions rather than merely with replay drift.
hypotheses.falsifier: Training-only causal or shadow-step analysis shows poor quantity alignment, or an arm produces replay drift without nonzero syntax/operation by update 200.
risks: Token embeddings carry the largest Q2.6 replay-drift and Fisher-weighted-drift diagnostics.
Output adaptation can memorize formatting without learning operation routing.
Tied embeddings/output weights can broaden the intervention unexpectedly.

hypotheses.family: optimizer, projection, or stopping-rule failure without changing the boundary
hypotheses.causal_mechanism: The top FFN may contain adequate representational capacity, but adaptive conditioning, a decisively misaligned projected direction, or a premature Pareto stop prevents acquisition.
hypotheses.expected_existing_trace_signature: Rejected/backtracked proposals, large or gate-aligned projection removal, collapsing gradient-to-step ratios, or continued improvement immediately before the stop would support this mechanism.
hypotheses.falsifier: A training-only shadow-step audit finds weak unprojected quantity alignment in the top FFN and no evidence that removed directions predict gate improvement; extending or retuning the same boundary then lacks a causal basis.
risks: Optimizer tuning can become an unconstrained search over a failed subspace.
Using public or language gates to tune the optimizer would leak evaluation authority.
A stop extension spends compute despite Q2.7's flat zero syntax/operation trajectory.

diagnostic_precondition.action: Add a training-only shadow-step audit before any new training authorization.
diagnostic_precondition.purpose: Measure groupwise new-task gradient energy, replay-gradient energy, their alignment, the proposed optimizer delta, and the post-profile/post-projection delta on frozen acquisition and replay batches.
diagnostic_precondition.authority_boundary: No BLiMP, TinyStories candidate set, promotion set, workflow dispatch, AWS instance, or parameter update is permitted by this research artifact.

ranked_interventions.reason: It directly compares graded stickiness with Q2.7's hard boundary, preserves distributed capacity seen in Q2.6, and has support from multiple independent method families.
It is a stronger isolation alternative if a stable training-only mask exists, but selection instability and implementation cost are higher.
It is the cheapest binary expansion and targets routing directly, but it retains the unestablished hard layer boundary.
It is simple, but differs little conceptually from the failed top-floor assumption and does not explain distributed Q2.6 movement.
It offers distributed capacity with immutable base weights, but changes architecture and is not itself a forgetting guarantee.
It is cheap but high-risk because embeddings dominate existing replay-risk diagnostics and useful causal alignment is unmeasured.
It deserves the zero-compute audit, but all accepted full-scale steps and flat gate results make an optimizer-only training rerun a poor first bet.

graded_profile_preregistration_candidate.granularity: parameter group for the first pilot; no per-weight claim
graded_profile_preregistration_candidate.old_behavior_importance: Mean squared gradients on the frozen direct-replay training set only, normalized by the median across eligible groups.
graded_profile_preregistration_candidate.new_task_relevance: Mean squared gradients on the frozen quantity-acquisition training set only, normalized by the median across eligible groups.
graded_profile_preregistration_candidate.plasticity_formula: p_g = 0.05 + 0.95 * N_g / (N_g + O_g + epsilon), where N_g and O_g are the normalized new-task relevance and old-behavior importance.
graded_profile_preregistration_candidate.profile_freeze: Compute once before training, hash the inputs and coefficients, and hold the profile fixed for the run.
graded_profile_preregistration_candidate.evaluation_firewall: BLiMP, TinyStories, promotion examples, and public candidate-gate results cannot influence importance, relevance, coefficients, floors, or stopping rules.
graded_profile_preregistration_candidate.weights_and_optimizer_moments: Apply p_g to the complete proposed parameter delta, including weight decay, before the replay-constrained weighted projection. Start optimizer moments from the same frozen initialization, never reuse moments across profiles, keep p_g fixed, and discard moments after the run. A future dynamic profile would require separate review and explicit moment-reset semantics.
graded_profile_preregistration_candidate.projection_geometry: Project the scaled proposed delta in the plasticity-weighted subspace so the replay correction cannot reopen nominally sticky coordinates without the same p_g multiplier.
graded_profile_preregistration_candidate.damage_migration_check: Report replay drift, Fisher-weighted drift, and accepted displacement by group and by replay slice; a good aggregate with a worsened slice is a failure.

cheapest_discriminating_pilot.new_arm: One seed-2 distributed graded-plasticity arm using the fixed profile above.
historical_controls: Q2.7 hard top-FFN control at the hash-bound run 31270819935
Q2.6 full-model reference at matched update checkpoints
cheapest_discriminating_pilot.quantity_compute_cost_basis: Q2.7 cost $0.484688888889 for 300 committed updates, or $0.161562962963 per 100 updates by linear extrapolation.
cheapest_discriminating_pilot.success_condition: At update 200, clear the unchanged quantity and per-slice replay gates and dominate Q2.7's matched outcome; freeze the candidate before any language evaluation.
cheapest_discriminating_pilot.failure_condition: At update 200, no jointly feasible quantity/replay checkpoint exists, or progress is purchased by moving replay damage into another slice or parameter group.
stop_conditions: Fail closed on any source, data, profile, contract, or trace hash mismatch.
Do not stop for scientific futility at update 100 solely because Q2.6 had not passed at that checkpoint.
Stop no later than 200 committed updates; no unregistered extension or profile retuning.
Do not run the $0.12 language gate unless a valid frozen quantity/replay candidate exists.
No promotion follows from the pilot; replication and promotion require separate authorization.

value_of_information.research_and_design_cost: The targeted 12-paper review and trace analysis are completed artifacts; exact agent-credit usage is unavailable and is not fabricated. Marginal implementation plus audit is estimated at 16-28 person-hours, which dominates the sub-dollar compute cost.
value_of_information.experiment_cost: The proposed pilot caps new compute at $0.62 including the conditional language screen; the quantity-only cap is $0.50.
value_of_information.decision_value: A success supports a distributed graded boundary for later replication; a failure retires this fixed estimator/profile before a broad multi-arm sweep. Either outcome distinguishes hard top-only undercapacity from a specific distributed-plasticity intervention.
value_of_information.compute_only_break_even: The $0.62 maximum is 48.1% of the existing $1.29 quantity-plus-conditional-language envelope. It pays for itself on compute alone if it has at least a 48.1% chance of preventing one otherwise uninformative full-envelope run; engineering time must be justified separately.
value_of_information.recommendation: Implement and verify the no-update shadow audit first. If it shows a stable cross-layer relevance/risk profile, open a separate protected experiment issue for exactly the 200-update graded pilot. Do not launch another hard top-only or optimizer-tuning run first.
value_of_information.further_literature_review: No further broad review is required for this fixed-profile pilot. A narrow follow-up is required if the design changes to dynamic masks, reused optimizer moments, jointly learned masks, or a new adapter architecture.
